messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT - Latency SLO breach detected on route `inference.generate` (p95 > 1200ms) across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Severity: P2. Paging on-call.
pagerduty: Paging @evan.ruiz (oncall) — escalation started
maria.chen: I see the alert too, pulling the router traces now
kevin.patel: looking at smart-router logs. lots of rapid policy decisions in the last 9m
evan.ruiz: acknowledged. is this the automatic SLO reroute kicking in? or did someone change policies?
tara.singh: automatic SLO reroute fired repeatedly. seems to flip between primary and a quantized fallback
maria.chen: pasted an excerpt from the decision log for one request:
```
[12:10:05] req=zx9 route=smart-router-a decision=primary model=model-13b-32k est=0.9s
[12:10:06] p95-window breached -> policy=slo-reroute action=failover target=model-13b-q4o
[12:10:06] fallback observed latency=1.9s -> still above threshold
[12:10:07] router flips back to primary
```
kevin.patel: q4o is quantized CPU variant — cheaper but bad tail latency for long contexts
evan.ruiz: matches what I see. many of these requests have context_length > 4k which kills q4o tail
satya.rao: any spikes in 5xx or client timeouts?
maria.chen: 5xx rate up from 0.15% to 1.2% in eu-west-1 over the last 12m. timeouts on token streams
IncidentBot: AUTOMATION SUMMARY — reroute_events=18 in 12m for policy slo-reroute; circuit_breaker not tripped
tara.singh: proposal: disable automatic SLO reroute for smart-router-a, temporarily pin to primary in eu-west-1 while we investigate. thoughts?
evan.ruiz: agree. disable reroute to avoid flip-flop. but pin TTL needs automatic rollback and capacity watch
kevin.patel: command to disable reroute:
```
curl -X POST https://control.internal/api/policies/smart-router-a/actions \
  -d '{"action":"disable_slo_reroute","reason":"failover oscillation"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
evan.ruiz: executing in 30s. I'll also open a temporary pin for eu-west-1 -> model-13b-32k
maria.chen: remember to add a short TTL to the pin so we don't forget
IncidentBot: ACTION — op=disable_slo_reroute id=op-77421 by evan.ruiz timestamp=2351234672
evan.ruiz: done. reroute disabled. monitoring p95 now
kevin.patel: immediate effect: p95 in eu-west-1 dropping from ~1.2s to ~0.85s
maria.chen: primary is starting to show higher queue depth — queue_depth up 2.5x, CPU on primary saturating at 88%
satya.rao: risk: pin fixes churn but could overload primary. can we apply a temporary client concurrency cap to reduce queueing?
tara.singh: applying soft concurrency cap for route inference.generate in eu-west-1
```
POST /internal/configs/concurrency
{"route":"inference.generate","region":"eu-west-1","max_in_flight":100}
```
kevin.patel: cap applied. p95 now ~720ms and error rate trending down
maria.chen: customer-impact note for CS: enterprise customers in EU with long-context requests saw elevated latency and some dropped streams between 12:10-12:50 UTC. No data loss. Root cause likely mismatch between reroute policy and variant selection (context-unaware policy picking q4o)
evan.ruiz: root cause hypothesis: the SLO-triggered policy lacks a selector for context_length and for variant-level tail behavior — it blindly picks the cheapest compatible variant, which performs poorly for long contexts, inducing repeated p95 breaches and reroutes -> oscillation
tara.singh: immediate mitigations completed: (1) disabled automatic SLO reroute for smart-router-a (op-77421), (2) pinned eu-west-1 to primary with TTL 20m, (3) applied concurrency cap to smooth queues
kevin.patel: follow-ups: add context_length predicate to reroute policy, introduce cooldown/hysteresis on p95-triggered actions, emit variant-level p95 metrics to alerting, run long-context perf tests for quantized variants
maria.chen: filing incident ticket and postmortem tag: slo-reroute-longcontext-quant
IncidentBot: UPDATE — severity reduced to P3 (mitigations applied); paging suppressed
pagerduty: AcknowledGED by oncall shift: tara.singh
evan.ruiz: handing off to tara now. I'm stepping off pager for the incident
tara.singh: I'll own the follow-ups for policy change and confirm tests for q4o
customer-success-bot: CS request: please provide a short non-technical summary for affected customers — timeline + actions taken
maria.chen: drafting CS blurb and will post to #customer-success
kevin.patel: internal TODOs: add unit tests for policy selector, add integration test for reroute hysteresis, update rollout docs
tara.singh: setting reminders: follow-up ticket assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml, due in 5 business days
IncidentBot: RESOLVED — incident duration 40m; final eu-west-1 p95=680ms; actions & owners recorded
